description: SereneDB test-config for DuckDB core's own test tree. Every entry is a known SereneDB divergence from upstream DuckDB, not a flake -- see tests/duckdb/README.md.

skip_tests.reason: There is no runtime extension loader: SereneDB builds with DISABLE_EXTENSION_LOAD and links its extension set statically, so `Binder::Bind(LoadStatement&)` raises `Not implemented Error: INSTALL|LOAD is not supported by SereneDB` for any extension that is not linked in (tracked in https://github.com/serenedb/serenedb/issues/887). Every file below stops at that refusal, and each one tests the loader itself or what only a loaded extension provides. (1) Features of a demo extension loaded by path, `LOAD '{BUILD_DIRECTORY}/test/extension/*.duckdb_extension'`: concurrent_load_extension, consistent_semicolon_extension_parse, explicit_extension_schema_testing, load_test_alias, reset_global_extension_option, test_alias_point, test_custom_type_modifier_cast, test_extensible_filter, test_function_named_args, test_tags, window_extension, test_custom_type_modifier, aliasing, quack_peeling, load_extension_capi_v2, test_function_args_kwargs, volatile_aggregate, load_use_extension_one_query. (2) The installer and the loader: install_extension and install_extension_httpfs expect download failures naming https://extensions.duckdb.org, load_error the `motherduk` -> `motherduck` suggestion, load_extension `IO Error: Extension ... not found` for `LOAD 'asdf'`, extension_repositories and extension_repository_not_autoloaded installs from custom repositories. (3) The loader's security gates: checked_load and load_arbitrary_path expect `Permission Error: DuckDB extensions are files ending with '.duckdb_extension'`, allowed_directories_install expects allowed_directories to govern the extension directory. (4) create_secret_persistence_no_client_context, whose `INSTALL bogus FROM 'http://example.com'` after a restart is how it initialises the secret manager without a ClientContext.

SereneDB parses one fixed SQL grammar (refactor(parser): one fixed grammar, no parser, grammar or dialect extensions): parser overrides, grammar extensions and dialects are gone, with the allow_parser_override_extension and current_dialect settings and the duckdb_dialects() function, and the demo extensions that provided them no longer build. test/extension/loadable_parser_override.test tests the parser override, test/extension/test_loadable_grammar_extension.test a grammar extension (pipe syntax), test/extension/test_loadable_dialect_extension.test a selectable dialect, and test/sql/table_function/duckdb_dialects.test duckdb_dialects() and current_dialect.

search_path follows PostgreSQL: a string literal is one schema name, so `SET search_path = 'a,b'` names the schema `a,b` (verified on PG 18, where SHOW search_path then reads "a,b"), and the entries are not validated. Both files test DuckDB's own reading of a search_path string as a quoted, comma-separated list. test/sql/catalog/test_set_search_path.test builds most of its cases on `SET SEARCH_PATH = 'test,test2'` meaning two schemas, and expects `SET SEARCH_PATH = 'does_not_exist'` to fail. test/sql/catalog/quoted_search_path.test expects `'"sch,ema""name"'` to parse into the schema `sch,ema"name` and `'"unterminated'` to be rejected.

SereneDB divides FLOAT, DOUBLE and DECIMAL values by IEEE 754, as docs/compatibility/core-sql-compatibility.md documents (`1.0 / 0.0` is Infinity, where PostgreSQL raises). integer_division rewrites every `/` to `//`, so `//` on FLOAT and DOUBLE follows `/`, and `//` on DECIMAL binds the DOUBLE overload: `7::DECIMAL(4,1) // 0::DECIMAL(4,1)` returns `inf` where the file expects `Division by zero`, and neither TRY nor error_on_division_by_zero=false turns that into NULL. The integer and unsigned iterations of the file pass.
